links.note: Which of the two paired texts is about a seagull - 'His First Flight'. The item tests knowing which story is which, which is 24150's pairing.
That 'His First Flight' is the seagull story, distinguishing it from the pilot's story in the same chapter.
The sight of food maddened him - hunger, not courage, is what moves him. 24156 states exactly that.
The sight of food maddened him - the necessity that finally overcomes his fear.
What urged him into his first flight - hunger and the sight of fish, not courage. That is 24156.
What urged his first flight - hunger and the fish, so necessity rather than the family's calling (24154).
Why his mother stopped midway with the fish - to push him to fly out of hunger. Necessity as the motive.
Why his mother halted with the fish - to make hunger do the work his courage could not.
What the seagull pretended - that he was falling asleep, to draw his family's notice while too afraid to fly.
The seagull pretending to fall asleep on his ledge - a device of his fear, so 24153.
The pilot was flying from France to England - the journey 24158 describes.
The pilot's route, France to England, in his old Dakota.
Which control station he contacted - Paris. A stage of the pilot's journey.
The control station he called - Paris, before entering the cloud.
The risk the pilot took - flying his old Dakota straight into the storm. 24158 names that storm cloud.
The risk taken - flying the old Dakota into the storm rather than turning back.
Which instruments stopped working in the storm - both compass and radio. Part of the pilot's journey into the cloud.
Both compass and radio failing inside the storm - the pilot's predicament.
What the pilot was not sorry about - flying into the storm and the risk it carried. His own account of the journey.
What the pilot was not sorry about - the decision to fly into the cloud.
Which instrument failed first - the compass. A detail of the flight into the storm.
The compass failing before the radio - the sequence of the pilot's troubles.
The name of the aeroplane the pilot flew - the Dakota, named in 24158.
The pilot's aircraft, an old Dakota - 24158's subject.
The pilot was not able to see anything - inside the storm cloud on his journey.
Unable to see anything once inside the cloud - a stage of the flight.
The direction in which the black aeroplane turned - north, when it told him to follow. That guide is 24159.
The black aeroplane turning north for him to follow - the mysterious guide's instruction.
Whether your parents ever pushed you to do something you were too scared to try - the counterpart of the seagull family's calling, scolding and threatening.
His parents perfecting his brothers and sisters in the art of flying - the family's instruction and example, which is 24154.
Who was alone on the ledge - the young seagull. 24153 opens with him alone there.
Why he stood on one leg with his eyes closed - to get his family's attention while still too afraid to fly.
One day passed and nobody came near him to help - his isolation on the ledge, which is 24153.
Write about your own first attempts at a skill such as cycling or swimming - the parallel the chapter draws with the seagull's first flight.
'I'll take the risk' - what the risk was and why the narrator took it: flying the Dakota into the storm cloud.
The narrator's experience flying the aeroplane into the storm - the journey into the cloud.
'Adversity reveals character' - two traits of the narrator shown by the flight into the storm.
What Forsyth thought when he called Paris Control - a stage of the journey before the cloud closed in.
What the narrator felt while flying over France back to England - the opening leg of the pilot's journey.
The reply from Paris Control and how he reacted - the pilot's journey before the storm.
